or $(2,1,1)$. An edge $s_it_j$ on $\{1,3\}$ excludes the
first choice, and one on $\{2,3\}$ excludes the second.
Retaining $\Psi_1$, $B$ and one such bridge, or one such
edge on each pair, therefore gives a nontoroidal subgraph.
By minimality, it is $G$.

Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:mohar} to $B\cup C_0$, where
$C_0=abdca$. Its auxiliary graph is three-connected by
\cite[Lemma~4.2]{Mohar1994}, applied to the $C_0$-bridge
$B$ in the three-connected graph $G+E(C_0)$. Thus outcome
(c) does not occur. Outcome (a) would give disjoint
$a$--$d$ and $b$--$c$ paths with internal vertices in
$D$, contrary to Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order}.
Hence $B$ contains a tripod.

Some attachment path of the tripod is nontrivial.
Otherwise removing its three attachments leaves two
disjoint trees in $D$. Join them by a shortest path
in $D$ and contract to two adjacent vertices, each
adjacent to all three attachments. Together with
$\Psi_1$, this gives a $K_5$ minor~\supp{W8}.

Since the fourth attachment has a neighbor in connected $D$,
take a path $P$ from it to a vertex of the tripod in $D$,
with internal vertices in $D$ and meeting the tripod only
at its last vertex. Contract the unused vertices of $D$
onto the tripod and $P$. Shorten the tripod as in the
proof of Lemma~\ref{endpoint:primitive}, retaining $P$
and choosing the attachment path through its last vertex
as the nontrivial one if there is such a path. Shorten
$P$ to an edge. This gives $T(g)$ on the tripod's
attachments, with the fourth attachment adjacent to
$u$, $p'$ or $q'$.

Shorten another four-attachment component in the same
way, or a three-attachment component to $T(g')$ by
Lemma~\ref{dis:exterior-triangles}. Each retained $T$
has nonplanar triangle completion, so the reduced bridges
still cannot be drawn in simple faces. The shortened
graph remains nontoroidal and hence equals $G$ by
minimality. In particular, a bridge on $s_i,t_i,v$
is $T(s_i)$ or $T(t_i)$, since $T(v)$ has a degree-three
vertex adjacent to both ends of $s_it_i$.

Up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$ and the indices $1,2$, the
fourth attachment of $B$ is $c$ and the tripod attaches
at $a,b,d$. If $g=d$, one of $p',q'$ has neighborhood
$\{a,b,u\}$, contrary to
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). If $c$ is
adjacent to $p'$, or symmetrically $q'$, the paths
$auq'd$ and $bp'c$ for $g=a$, or $aq'd$ and
$bup'c$ for $g=b$, contradict
Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order}. If $c$ is adjacent to
$u$ and $g=b$, the paths $ap'd$ and $buc$ give the
same contradiction. Thus $g=a$, $u$ is adjacent to
$a,c$, and $p',q'$ are adjacent to $b,d,u$.
The only other form interchanges $A_1,A_2$, and the same
description applies to the other four-attachment
component after relabeling. Every resulting graph has
a proper minor failing all twelve choices~\supp{E2}, a contradiction.

vertex names: a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t2, e = s3, f = t3; twins p, q on {a, c, e} and r, z on {b, d, f}; the paths P1, P2, P3 are the edges ab, cd, ef. The bridge B has interior vertices u, p', q' as in the text. The other component, when there is one, has interior vertices u'', p'', q''.
the graphs: Psi_1, the bridge B in one of its two forms, and exactly one of: another three-attachment component, shortened to T(g') with g' an end of the edge ab, cd or ef in its attachment triple (8 triples, 2 choices of g'); a four-attachment component on {a,b,e,f} or {c,d,e,f} of the same form as B (2 forms); or one of the edges af, eb together with one of cf, ed. With the two forms of B this gives 32 + 8 + 8 = 48 graphs.
how a choice fails: For each choice (k,x,y) of Lemma 4.2, the faces are the pair of simple faces (attachments V(P_i) ∪ V(P_j), test graph with auxiliary edges s_i s_j, t_i t_j), the repeated face (attachments V(P_k) ∪ {s_x, t_y}, auxiliary edges s_k s_x, t_k t_y) and the two faces of (iii) (attachments {s_k, s_x'} and {t_k, t_y'}). A choice fails when some Psi_1-bridge has its attachments in no face, or when every assignment of bridges to faces with their attachments makes some test graph nonplanar (Lemma 4.3). Each such assignment is listed with a Kuratowski subgraph.
